Appendix — V7 — klagen + houden van + zin in (12 images)

Grok-prompt, letterlijk
Same Voorzetselpaden house style as the delivered A0–A2 set. Twelve separate
images, 2:3 portrait, cobalt #2B50C8 only, brush line, plain white, no text or
numbers. Exact filenames, in this order:

1. klagen-over-eten.png — klagen over (to complain about)
   Scene: person at a table pushing a plate away with a displeased face,
   speaking to a companion; no waiter.
   Must read: complaining about the food.
   Avoid: complaining to staff (klagen bij); waiting for food (wachten op eten).

2. klagen-over-kou.png — klagen over
   Scene: person shivering and gesturing to a companion, coat pulled tight.
   Must read: complaining about the cold.
   Avoid: suffering silently (last hebben van kou); protecting against cold.

3. klagen-over-weg.png — klagen over
   Scene: person pointing at a pothole or broken road surface, speaking to a
   companion.
   Must read: complaining about the road.
   Avoid: complaining to an official (klagen bij); road works.

4. klagen-bij-leidinggevende.png — klagen bij (to complain to)
   Scene: employee at a desk complaining to a manager who sits listening.
   Must read: complaining to a manager.
   Avoid: complaining about a thing to a peer (klagen over); a performance
   review.

5. klagen-bij-receptie.png — klagen bij
   Scene: guest at a hotel reception desk speaking to a receptionist.
   Must read: complaining at reception.
   Avoid: checking in; complaining to a friend.

6. klagen-bij-winkelier.png — klagen bij
   Scene: customer at a shop counter holding a faulty item, speaking to the
   shopkeeper.
   Must read: complaining to the shopkeeper.
   Avoid: buying; complaining to a friend.

7. houden-van-partner.png — houden van (to love)
   Scene: couple embracing calmly.
   Must read: loving a partner.
   Avoid: a greeting; a gift.

8. houden-van-kat.png — houden van
   Scene: person cradling a relaxed cat, affectionate.
   Must read: loving a cat.
   Avoid: caring for a pet (zorgen voor); a dog (existing scene).

9. houden-van-muziek.png — houden van
   Scene: person with headphones, eyes closed, blissful, slightly swaying.
   Must read: loving music.
   Avoid: listening for information; a phone call.

10. zin-in-taart.png — zin in (to feel like)
    Scene: person leaning toward a cake on a table, hands ready, eager.
    Must read: craving cake.
    Avoid: eating; baking (bezig zijn met koken).

11. zin-in-eten.png — zin in
    Scene: person at a table looking eagerly toward a full plate or the kitchen.
    Must read: wanting food.
    Avoid: waiting for food (wachten op eten); complaining.

12. zin-in-zwemmen.png — zin in
    Scene: person in swimwear at the edge of water, eager, ready to go in.
    Must read: feeling like a swim.
    Avoid: actually swimming; fear of water.

CROSS-CHECKS — draw these together
- klagen over (1–3) vs klagen bij (4–6): over is a complaint about a thing or
  situation, spoken to a companion or peer. bij is a complaint directed to
  staff or authority at a desk or counter. No over scene may have a service
  counter; no bij scene may be a peer-to-peer chat.
- 1 is not wachten op eten and not tevreden zijn met eten: the plate is rejected
  and the face is displeased. 2 is spoken complaint, not silent shivering (last
  hebben van kou).
- houden van (7–9) is affection: embrace, cradling, bliss. It is not caregiving
  (zorgen voor) and not curiosity (geinteresseerd in).
- zin in (10–12) is immediate desire: the person leans toward or reaches for the
  thing. It is not future anticipation (uitkijken naar) and not waiting.

VALIDATION
For every image: at 64 × 64 the idea must still be nameable; cobalt only; no
text, numbers, arrows or readable signs; plain white; one idea. Check each pair
side by side: the two must remain clearly different and neither may suggest the
other chunk. Return only the listed files and name any ambiguous silhouette.

Appendix — V8 — bang + zeggen/vertellen (9 images)

Grok-prompt, letterlijk
Same Voorzetselpaden house style as the delivered A0–A2 set. Nine separate
images, 2:3 portrait, cobalt #2B50C8 only, brush line, plain white, no text or
numbers. Exact filenames, in this order:

1. bang-voor-spin.png — bang voor (afraid of)
   Scene: person recoiling from a small spider on the floor, hands up, leaning
   away.
   Must read: afraid of a spider.
   Avoid: disgust without fear; stepping on it.

2. bang-voor-hoogte.png — bang voor
   Scene: person at a high edge, clinging to a railing, looking down nervously.
   Must read: afraid of heights.
   Avoid: looking out of a window (kijken uit); jumping.

3. bang-voor-onweer.png — bang voor
   Scene: person huddled under a blanket indoors while a storm cloud and
   lightning show outside a window.
   Must read: afraid of the storm.
   Avoid: protection against rain (beschermen tegen); a cosy scene.

4. zeggen-tegen-buur.png — zeggen tegen (to say to)
   Scene: two people at a low fence; one leans in and says one short thing,
   shown as a single small speech shape; the other listens.
   Must read: saying something to a neighbour.
   Avoid: a long story (vertellen aan); arguing.

5. zeggen-tegen-collega.png — zeggen tegen
   Scene: two people at a desk; one turns and says a short remark, shown as a
   single small speech shape; the other looks up.
   Must read: saying something to a colleague.
   Avoid: a discussion (praten met); a meeting.

6. zeggen-tegen-kleinkind.png — zeggen tegen
   Scene: older person bends to a grandchild and says one short instruction,
   shown as a single small speech shape; the child looks up.
   Must read: saying something to a grandchild.
   Avoid: a long story (vertellen aan); scolding (boos op).

7. vertellen-aan-buur.png — vertellen aan (to tell to)
   Scene: the same fence and the same two figures as 4; one gestures broadly and
   a long blank ribbon or scroll shape rises between them; the neighbour
   listens attentively.
   Must read: telling a story to a neighbour.
   Avoid: a single short speech shape (zeggen tegen); two-way chatter.

8. vertellen-aan-collega.png — vertellen aan
   Scene: the same desk and the same two figures as 5; a long blank ribbon or
   scroll shape between them; the colleague listens.
   Must read: telling a long story to a colleague.
   Avoid: a brief remark (zeggen tegen); a meeting.

9. vertellen-aan-kleinkind.png — vertellen aan
   Scene: the same figures as 6; the older person gestures expressively and a
   long blank ribbon or scroll shape rises; the grandchild listens.
   Must read: telling a story to a grandchild.
   Avoid: a short instruction (zeggen tegen); a book with readable pages.

CROSS-CHECKS — draw these together
- bang voor (1–3) is fear: recoiling, clinging or huddling. It is not caution
  (uitkijken voor) and not protection (beschermen tegen).
- zeggen tegen (4–6) vs vertellen aan (7–9): zeggen is one short utterance, one
  small speech shape. vertellen is an extended story, a long ribbon or scroll.
  4↔7, 5↔8 and 6↔9 are matched pairs: same two figures, same camera, same
  setting. Change only the speech shape and the listener's posture. The short
  versus long distinction must survive at 64 × 64.
- zeggen tegen is not praten met: only one person speaks. vertellen aan is not
  praten over: there is no topic object, the story itself is the focus.

VALIDATION
For every image: at 64 × 64 the idea must still be nameable; cobalt only; no
text, numbers, arrows or readable signs; plain white; one idea. Check each pair
side by side: the two must remain clearly different and neither may suggest the
other chunk. Return only the listed files and name any ambiguous silhouette.

Appendix — V9 — beschermen + komen door + komen uit (9 images)

Grok-prompt, letterlijk
Same Voorzetselpaden house style as the delivered A0–A2 set. Nine separate
images, 2:3 portrait, cobalt #2B50C8 only, brush line, plain white, no text or
numbers. Exact filenames, in this order:

1. beschermen-tegen-zon.png — beschermen tegen (to protect against)
   Scene: person calm under a wide hat or parasol, a strong sun shape above.
   Must read: protected from the sun.
   Avoid: rain (existing scene); sunbathing.

2. beschermen-tegen-wind.png — beschermen tegen
   Scene: person calm behind a wall, holding a coat closed, wind bending a tree
   beyond.
   Must read: protected from the wind.
   Avoid: fear of a storm (bang voor onweer); rain.

3. beschermen-tegen-hond.png — beschermen tegen
   Scene: person stepping between a child and a barking dog, one arm out as a
   barrier; the dog is on the other side.
   Must read: protecting a child from a dog.
   Avoid: fear of the dog (bang voor); anger at the dog (boos op).

4. komen-door-zon.png — komen door (to be caused by)
   Scene: person hot and wilted, fanning themselves and pointing up at the sun;
   hat in the other hand.
   Must read: the sun caused it.
   Avoid: enjoying the sun; an umbrella or parasol (beschermen tegen).

5. komen-door-storm.png — komen door
   Scene: person leaning into the wind, dishevelled, pointing at a bending tree.
   Must read: the storm caused it.
   Avoid: a wall or barrier (beschermen tegen); calm weather.

6. komen-door-hond.png — komen door
   Scene: person with muddy clothes pointing at a dog; the dog stands nearby.
   Must read: the dog caused it.
   Avoid: anger at the dog (boos op); caring for the dog.

7. komen-uit-winkel.png — komen uit (to come from)
   Scene: person stepping out of a shop door with a shopping bag, mid-stride.
   Must read: coming out of a shop.
   Avoid: getting out of a vehicle (stappen uit); going into the shop.

8. komen-uit-kantoor.png — komen uit
   Scene: person leaving an office building with a briefcase, the door behind
   them.
   Must read: coming out of the office.
   Avoid: working there (werken bij); stepping out of a vehicle (stappen uit).

9. komen-uit-keuken.png — komen uit
   Scene: person emerging from a kitchen door carrying a tray, mid-step.
   Must read: coming out of the kitchen.
   Avoid: cooking (bezig zijn met koken); waiting for food.

CROSS-CHECKS — draw these together
- beschermen tegen (1–3) vs komen door (4–6): protection is an active barrier
  (hat, wall, arm) between the person and the threat, and the person is calm or
  shielded. komen door shows the cause and an affected person pointing at it;
  there is no barrier.
- 1↔4 sun, 2↔5 wind/storm and 3↔6 dog are matched pairs: same threat, same
  camera, one protected and one affected. Keep the threat identical in each
  pair. 3 is protection in action, not fear (bang voor hond).
- komen uit (7–9) is emerging from a place or building. It is not stepping down
  out of a vehicle (stappen uit). 7 must not look like 33 werken bij winkel;
  8 must not look like 32 werken bij kantoor.

VALIDATION
For every image: at 64 × 64 the idea must still be nameable; cobalt only; no
text, numbers, arrows or readable signs; plain white; one idea. Check each pair
side by side: the two must remain clearly different and neither may suggest the
other chunk. Return only the listed files and name any ambiguous silhouette.

Must read

Avoid
getting out of a vehicle (stappen uit); going into the shop.

uit vs stappen uit
zwak beeld
